body: Right now the fraction will not show a decimal if the step is a whole number. Not sure if this is what would be best so im open to feedback.

While I really like the change, I even liked the old PR back then, I think it should be implemented the same way as in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103998.

That is, a `format` property, which enable developers to really do basically every kind of formatting needed. And it matches the `SpinBox` API, which IMO we should aim for (consistency with other GUI controls).

I have implemented it quite closely following https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103998 though there is 1 small difference: If left empty it acts just like the old show_percentage being false. This is inconsistent with the other PR which would then set it to be the default. Here this is not an issue since the default value is set correctly. If it is preferred that a separate visible bool is exposed then I think it should be something new since this does more then just show or hide a percentage now. At the same time they would effectively have the same use so I wonder if there is a way to deprecate show_percentage and have it just point to the new variable if it is edited?

Another thing to note is the docs here state that the ProgressBar will display `Invalid` if the format is not valid but it actually displays `<Invalid>` just like the other PR. Unfortunately I am unable to add this to the docs as it does not seem escape characters are supported? Though I suppose its a bit more correct then the spinbox docs which state it will show "ERROR" (This should probably be corrected in a seperate PR)


### Now for some additional questions since im very new to the godot codbase:
 - I also wanted to ask in the original a bit more about the `_validate_property` function and the bit I removed. I understand that the old code would lock this value in the editor if `indeterminate` is true but im not sure what `indeterminate` is or used for so im not sure if similar code should be added for this. I very easily could add the following:
```cpp
if (Engine::get_singleton()->is_editor_hint() && indeterminate && p_property.name == "format") {
	p_property.usage |= PROPERTY_USAGE_READ_ONLY;
}
```

 - `update_configuration_warnings` is called when format is set. If format for some reason is set via a script at runtime this likely introduces unnecessary many checks  and I would assume the dev has already made sure it all works. Would it be good to check `is_editor_hint` before calling this to make sure it only runs in the editor?
 
 - `get_minimum_size` even originally just inserted a placeholder and didnt insert the current value. I understand that this function likely ensures the ProgressBar is at least this size to display the message but wouldnt the actual current value need to be used here to ensure its 100% accurate? For example say `value` is some large number (`1000000`), and `%s` is the `format`. `get_minimum_size` would test it with a placeholder 1 at the moment leading to way too short of a space being allocated. On the other hand this is likely a rare case and introduces many duplicate string manipulation tasks so im not sure if that would be wanted for efficiency? Perhaps there is a better way. Or perhaps we do not care about the performance hit so much.

 - In the referenced PR it mostly made sense except for so many seemingly unrelated files like `audio_stream_import_settings.cpp` for example were changed to change the setter. I didn't see it but does something similar need to be done here?

Intermediate is a progress style. I think the new format text should be used there as well. The reason why `intermediate` did not show the percentage is because there is none. Intermediate is basically no progress, so no percentage can be shown.

With the `format` however, you may want to show something like `Initializing download...` while making the progress `intermediate`, and at one point you may turn it off and 'switch' to progress, where you might wanna change the `format` to something like `Download X / Y MB`, as an example.

> get_minimum_size

Could the `minimum_size` count in the format string? Maybe with a string such as `Downloaded %d / %d MB`, we could factor in the text and the `max_value` of the `ProgressBar`. Lets say it is 250, then the maximum would be: `Downloaded 250 / 250 MB` -- and if we can use that logic to calculate the min size, we might be good to go.

You might want to play around with `ProgressBar` to get more familiar with it. Maybe even check how it is used in the Engine to understand possible usecases -- this is just an example how `format` could be used together with `intermediate`.

Ok moved stuff around. Like was suggested I made it so that it pads for the max values input. This has the issue of where if I want to show `10/10` for example and thats the max value thats all good until you have a `9.95/10` which goes longer then the padding. Thats a small issue with the method I implemented. Also I do wonder what `get_minimum_size` size really does because at first I thought it would ensure that the size of the ProgressBar would always be big enough to fit the text but this has never been the case. I also made it so with Intermediate mode enabled you can set whatever text you want: Currently it still displays a warning even with Intermediate mode on. With it off it would display ``. I very much could make it so that all "Error states" show the plain text but that might be confusing (Though perhaps with the warning it wont be too bad? For now its like stated above.) Also Intermediate mode on will still show the correct formatting in percent for example if the format is `%d%%` but that seems fine.
From memory I think currently minimum size only accounts for the text height not the width.

> From memory I think currently minimum size only accounts for the text height not the width.

If this is the case it doesnt appear like these extra calculations matter at all? Any text will always be the same height in this check. It could be checked against a static string and it would still be just as good if this is true.

This also means that the biggest issue while still an issue makes no difference here in practice.
